title: Decide zoom semantics on mock canvases
goal: Zooming on the mock canvases changes the background grid but leaves the artwork exactly the same size, so the readout can say 260 percent while nothing looks any bigger. Someone needs to decide what zoom should mean here, and then every editing surface should behave that way.
notes:
Objective: creation-vision > editor-surfaces (needs a UX decision before any implementation). From study-tasks.json zoom-scales-grid-not-artwork. Zoom changes grid density but artwork stays the same size, so the readout can say 260 percent while the hero card renders at 1x. Honest fix: scale artwork by --zoom and counter-scale selection chrome by 1/--zoom. This changes what zoom means on every editor page: open a UX decision before implementing.

DROPPED 2026-08-24 (stage gate, not a judgment on the bug). Confirmed still real: canvas.css maps --zoom to grid cell size only; slider.js:157 sets it per .canvas. Artwork never scales. Re-file under creation-vision > editor-surfaces when that epic is staged now.
acceptance: A decision is opened and answered on whether zoom scales the artwork or only the grid
The chosen behaviour is implemented once in the shared canvas and holds on at least three editing pages at half, normal and double zoom
If artwork scales, selection outlines and handles stay the same thickness at every zoom level
